sullorsuaq-strait.name: Sullorsuaq Strait
sullorsuaq-strait.summary: Strait on Greenland's western coast, known in Danish as Vaigat.

nuussuaq-peninsula.name: Nuussuaq Peninsula
nuussuaq-peninsula.summary: A large peninsula in western Greenland, roughly 180 by 48 kilometres in size.

disko-island.name: Disko Island
disko-island.summary: Large island off western Greenland, the second-largest island belonging to Greenland and among the world's 100 largest islands.

greenlandian.name: Greenlandian
greenlandian.summary: The earliest stage of the Holocene Epoch, officially ratified in 2018, marked by rapid post-ice-age global warming until a cooling reversal called the 8.2-kiloyear event; rising seas turned regions like the British Isles into islands.

younger-dryas.name: Younger Dryas
younger-dryas.summary: A sudden cold phase from about 12,900 to 11,700 years ago that sharply cooled the Northern Hemisphere before rapid warming began the current era.

saqqaq-culture.name: Saqqaq culture
saqqaq-culture.summary: A Paleo-Inuit culture in southern Greenland, named after the settlement of Saqqaq, and the longest-residing culture in Greenland's history.

dorset-culture.name: Dorset culture
dorset-culture.summary: A Paleo-Eskimo culture in the North American Arctic, lasting from about 500 BCE until it died out by 1000–1500 CE, before the Thule (proto-Inuit) arrived. Inuit legends recall its people as the Tuniit.

thule-people.name: Thule people
thule-people.summary: The precursors of modern Inuit and Yupik peoples, who developed in coastal Alaska by 1000 CE, spread across the Arctic, and replaced the earlier Dorset culture by the 15th century.

alluttoq-island.name: Alluttoq Island
alluttoq-island.summary: Large, uninhabited island in western Greenland's Disko Bay, struck by two prehistoric megatsunamis around 5650 and 5350 BC with run-up heights over 200 feet.

komsa-culture.name: Komsa culture
komsa-culture.summary: A Mesolithic hunter-gatherer culture in northern Norway from around 10,000 BC, named after Mount Komsa where its remains were first found in 1925.

ahrensburg-culture.name: Ahrensburg culture
ahrensburg-culture.summary: A late Upper Paleolithic hunter culture in north-central Europe, around 12,900 to 11,700 years ago, that mastered bow-and-arrow hunting during the cold Younger Dryas period.

paleo-eskimo.name: Paleo-Eskimo
paleo-eskimo.summary: The peoples who inhabited the Arctic from Siberia to Greenland before the modern Inuit, with cultures developing from about 3900 BCE and the last, the Dorset, disappearing around 1500 CE.

anders-nummedal.name: Anders Nummedal
anders-nummedal.summary: A Norwegian archaeologist (1867–1944) who discovered the Fosna culture and, in 1925, the first traces of the related Komsa culture in Northern Norway.

fosna-hensbacka-culture.name: Fosna-Hensbacka
fosna-hensbacka-culture.summary: A Late Palaeolithic to early Mesolithic culture (about 8300-7300 BCE) along the coasts of Norway and Sweden.

varangerfjord.name: Varangerfjord
varangerfjord.summary: Norway's easternmost fjord, in Finnmark county near the Russian border, associated with early prehistoric coastal settlement in the region.
